title: Silence the ringing alarm clock
household_need: Notice that the alarm clock has gone off and switch it off for good with one press on its top.
instruction: The alarm clock on the counter will start ringing at an unpredictable time: its bells and hammer shake and the whole clock rattles. Wait until it rings, then silence it within 4.6 seconds: press the red button on top of its handle straight down, from above, about 5 mm, until it stays down. Then let go: it counts once nothing touches the button for 1 second. Do not touch the button before the alarm rings, and do not knock the clock over or push it more than 5 cm.
core_interventions: press the stop button on top of the clock straight down past its catch, then let go

process.state: alarm ringing or not; stop button latched or not
process.model: the alarm starts at ring_time and rings until the measured button travel reaches the catch (4 of 6 mm); the catch then holds the button down and the alarm stays off
process.cue: visual only (the policy has no audio): while it rings the hammer swings between the bells, the bells shiver and the clock twists +-5 deg about its vertical axis and hops 2 mm, changing every 0.04 s; all still again once silenced, and the red button stays down. The second hand ticks throughout.

timing.event: silenced = button travel >= 4 mm after the alarm started
timing.rule: loss = seconds of ringing; limit 15 / 4.6 / 1.4 s (easy / medium / hard)
timing.calibration: hard = max(t / 0.8, t + 0.3 s, 1 s) with t = 1.10 s, the reference oracle's slowest silencing from the ready pose over seeds 0-9; medium = sqrt(easy x hard); easy 15 s is a design choice (no source found for how long a wind-up alarm is left ringing)

physical: button pressed past its catch by robot contact after the alarm started
clock upright (tilt <= 30 deg) and within 5 cm of its place
completion.temporal: seconds of ringing within the tier limit

failures: button touched or pressed before the alarm rings
permitted: a late silencing still completes the task physically (timing fails)
arm_roles: right: button (single arm); the clock stands between the arms, so the left arm reaches it too
demo_guidance: The clock is a 0.35 kg free-standing rigid body (cylinder and box colliders); the button is a 5 g body on a sprung prismatic joint in the handle (300 N/m, 1.8 N at the stop), held down by a 3 N catch force once the alarm is off.

The oracle waits at the ready pose with closed jaws, moves the fingertips 3 cm above the button with the tool pitched 60 deg down (a straight-down tool does not reach this height), presses down at 6 cm/s until the travel reaches the stop, lifts off and returns.
Per seed the clock is shifted +-4 cm in x, +-3 cm in y and turned +-15 deg; the button is on its vertical axis.
open_items: the ringing is shown by motion of the rendered meshes only; the colliders stay still, and there is no sound
the stop button is authored: the Poly Haven model has none (top silencer buttons exist on some wind-up alarm clocks, e.g. a 1940 Westclox, collectorsweekly.com/stories/117)
